profile.headline: Embedded Software Engineer
profile.summary:
I am an Embedded Software Engineer, having completed my Master of Science degree in Computer Engineering at San Jose State University with a concentration in Embedded Systems.

Concurrent with my MS in Computer Engineering studies, I worked full time as a Software Engineer with Cohu, a semiconductor test equipment manufacturer. My team, comprised of engineers in the US and Taiwan, was responsible for the design, development, and integration of unit tests and drivers for new DSP, power, and digital instruments using C++. The projects and design patterns undertaken in my MS program enhanced the quality and efficiency of the code I delivered as a software engineer for Cohu. I also tapped into my background in electrical engineering to complement and accelerate my understanding of embedded systems, as my time management skills were put to the test.

I first joined Cohu as a Training Specialist immediately after completing my BS in Electrical Engineering at Cal Poly Polytechnic University. With pointers from a seasoned technical trainer, I was immediately immersed in conducting week-long training classes for application engineers on the use and trouble-shooting of C++ based tester software used in the automated test equipment semiconductor industry. I was quickly set free to conduct training on my own and had to tailor material to audiences of highly varied skill sets. Through these experiences, I developed technical training and interpersonal skills across a new audience of users each class. My rapid development did not go unnoticed at Cohu, and gave rise to my transfer to software engineering.

While at Cal Poly, I embraced the university’s Learn by Doing motto and joined the Underwater Robotics Club where I served as the Electrical Engineering Lead. The experiences on the team enhanced both my own engineering skill set and helped me build leadership skills, as I was called upon to delegate and supervise junior members of the team to manage a timeline of deliverables.

In my free time, I enjoy volleyball, lifting, swimming, climbing, 3D printing, gaming, and challenging myself with embedded projects - particularly in autonomous vehicles as mentioned in my post about my SJSU RC car project, found here: https://azuninoprojects.wordpress.com/2023/07/10/embedded-systems-applications-autonomous-rc-car/.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Responsibilities:
• Design, develop, and integrate software and unit tests for new instrument device drivers
• Quickly debug and root-cause bugs and software regressions that arise
• Support new tools, hardware, and system features for ATE operating systems
• Support software releases using C++ with Clearcase and Linux platform

Achievements:
• Worked with marketing, hardware, and firmware teams to design and integrate several new instruments - DSP, power, and digital - to test semiconductor devices.

positions.title: Training Specialist
positions.description:
Responsibilities:
• Conduct and evaluate application and maintenance training courses.
• Create test program examples to demonstrate instrument functionalities.
• Provide customer training on and off-site for Cohu's automated test equipment (ATE).
• Develop training material for usage on test system instruments.

Achievements:
• Created custom PCBs and provided internal trainings to save major costs to the company.

positions.title: Hardware Electrical Engineering Lead
positions.locationName: San Luis Obispo County, California, United States
positions.description:
Responsibilities:
• Lead the electrical team in building an underwater robot following MATE competition specifications
• Assign new members to projects tailored to their interests and answered questions
• Plan and organize meetings and events to attract new members and keep team chemistry

Achievements:
• Designed and calculated trace widths, manufactured, and brought up a power board managing all power inputs and outputs for the system
• Created a waterproof camera enclosure with 180 degree rotation control while operating underwater
• Enhanced the top-side control unit by reworking the enclosure, rewiring, and stabilizing all connections

Links:

Introduction to the club:
• https://azuninoprojects.wordpress.com/2017/09/27/robotics-club-urov-for-competition/

Waterproof camera enclosure project:
• https://azuninoprojects.wordpress.com/2017/06/04/robotics-club-urov-camera-encasement/
positions.insights: Skills: Embedded Systems · Autodesk EAGLE · Leadership · Git · Embedded Software · Linux

positions.title: Electrical Engineering Intern
positions.description:
Responsibilities
• Develop a custom PCB given a set of specifications determined by mentors
• Host design reviews and brainstorm improvements to electrical subsystems with the electrical engineering team

Achievements
• Produced a flight recorder PCB using Altium Designer and wrote the firmware to interrupt when a crash is detected and store data from different sensors
• Tested and brought up a new revision of an AC junction box to decrease power loss and improve readability of the PCB
• Received training on the following tools to test new ideas and designs reflected in my internship: lathe, mill, and band saw
positions.insights: Skills: Embedded Systems · Software Development · C++ · Python · Embedded Software · Altium Designer

honors.title: Senior Project Ingenuity Award
honors.description: The research, design, and implementation of the sustainable security system my team and I created for our capstone project resulted in this award on our department graduation day. Over the course of a year, our team collaborated on a working physical prototype that was a new niche of the security and sustainability market. With the ability to charge itself, the security device was best placed on or next to a window for solar energy, and an effective location to determine break-ins and also catastrophic events.
honors.issuer: Issued by Department of Electrical Engineering · Jun 2019

honors.title: Academic All-American
honors.description: An award given to athletes of the water polo community who achieved a GPA greater than 3.6.  Received both in 2014 and 2015.
honors.issuer: Issued by USA Water Polo · Jan 2015

projects.title: CMPE 243 - Embedded Systems Applications
projects.description:
Meh-Sla Automotive, the autonomous RC car my team and I tore apart and rebuilt using Preetpal Kang's SJ2 microcontroller boards. 

It utilizes four SJ2 boards, each with their own functionality (Motor, Driver, Sensor, Geological Controller), to navigate autonomously to a programmed destination using a mobile phone application.

projects.title: ME 405 - Nerf Gun Bingo Bash
projects.description: In my technical elective class, ME405 - Mechatronics, the final project grouped up three creative engineers, either Mechanical or Electrical, and assigned them the task of creating a mounted assembly which can hold a Nerf gun.  It should shoot at a given coordinate and be fully functional with no physical interference except the input of the coordinates in a user interface designed by our team.
